- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slope or cap upward bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >75), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply downward drag or lagged mean reversion after peak.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and price is rising, model may overfit trend; cap forecast growth or introduce slight downward bias to avoid overcorrection.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70), model often fails to adjust; apply smoothing or weighted average with recent low sentiment.
- If model forecast is rising steadily but true outcome shows volatility or reversal, reduce forecast slope or introduce sentiment-weighted volatility buffer.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the window; apply linear decay or sentiment-adjusted smoothing to reduce initial bias.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows, model may misread momentum; use sentiment-weighted moving average to dampen false momentum signals.
